part.discoveredAndDoubleCheck.title: Discovered check and double check
part.discoveredAndDoubleCheck.summary: A piece steps out of another one's way and the check comes from behind: the piece that moves is free to attack. With two checks at once, the king must move.
ex.dc.TofJt: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.dc.TofJt.hint: The knight on g5 stands between your queen and the black king. From which square does it attack a black piece?
ex.dc.TofJt.solution: 19.Nxe6+! captures the pawn and opens the g-file: the queen on g3 gives a discovered check, and the knight attacks the queen on d8. After 19...Kh8, 20.Nxd8 captures the queen. With 19.Nxf7+?, it is also a discovered check, but the king recaptures the knight, and the black queen stays where it is.
ex.dc.PEIu4: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.dc.PEIu4.hint: The rook on c1 and the black king stand on the same file. Which white piece is between them?
ex.dc.PEIu4.solution: 23.Nxd5+! captures the pawn and opens the c-file: the rook on c1 gives a discovered check, and the knight attacks the bishop on e7. After 23...Kb8, 24.Nxe7 captures the bishop. With 23.Nxb5+?, it is also a discovered check, but from b5 the knight attacks no piece, and the game is level.
ex.dc.WZXOC: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dc.WZXOC.hint: The knight on e5 stands between your rook on e6 and the white king. Look for the square from which it also gives check.
ex.dc.WZXOC.solution: 40...Nc4+! gives check with the knight and opens the e-file for the rook on e6: it is a double check, and the knight attacks the rook on b2. The king must move, and after 41.Kd4, 41...Nxb2 captures the rook. With 40...Nxd3+?, only the rook gives check, and the king recaptures the knight.
ex.dc.GoNZ8: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dc.GoNZ8.hint: The knight on f3 stands between your queen on e4 and the white king. Look for the square from which it gives check and attacks a queen.
ex.dc.GoNZ8.solution: 35...Ne1+! gives check with the knight and opens the diagonal of the queen on e4: it is a double check, and the knight attacks the queen on d3. The king must move, and after 36.Kg1, 36...Nxd3 captures the queen. With 35...Qxd3?, the bishop on f1 recaptures, and only White still has a queen, the one on c8.
ex.dc.y3hCF: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.dc.y3hCF.hint: Before moving the rook on c7, check what it wins once the king steps out of check. There is a check that leaves the black king without a square.
ex.dc.y3hCF.solution: 18.Rd1+! gives check with the rook from h1, and the black king only has e8. After 18...Ke8, 19.Rc8# is mate. With 18.Rxb7+?, the rook on c7 moves away and uncovers the check of the bishop on b6, but the king goes to c8 or e8, and the rook on b7 wins nothing: Black stays a piece up. Capturing the bishop would be worse for Black: 18...Rxb6? 19.Rxb6.
ex.dc.Uks6M: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dc.Uks6M.hint: The bishop on c8 and the white king stand on the same diagonal. Which black piece is between them?
ex.dc.Uks6M.solution: 23...Nxc5+! captures the pawn and opens the diagonal of the bishop on c8 to the king on h3: it is a discovered check, and the knight attacks the queen on b3. After 24.Kh2, 24...Nxb3 captures the queen. With 23...Nf6+?, it is also a discovered check, but from f6 the knight does not attack the queen, and White is better.
ex.dc.PLbiq: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.dc.PLbiq.hint: One of your pieces stands between your queen and the black king. Look for its move that also attacks a black piece.
ex.dc.PLbiq.solution: 23.Ne7+! gives check with the knight and opens the diagonal of the queen on b3: it is a double check, and the knight attacks the queen on f5. The king must move, and after 23...Kh8, 24.Nxf5 captures the queen. With 23.Nf6+?, it is also a double check, but from f6 the knight does not attack the queen, and Black is better.
ex.dc.9pocB: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.dc.9pocB.hint: One of your pieces stands between your rook and the white king. Look for its move that also attacks a white piece.
ex.dc.9pocB.solution: 54...Nf4+! gives check with the knight and opens the d-file for the rook on d8: it is a double check, and the knight attacks the rook on g6. After 55.Ke4, 55...Nxg6 captures the rook. With 54...Nb4+?, it is also a double check, but from b4 the knight does not attack the rook, and White is better.
ex.dc.HAwiT: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.dc.HAwiT.hint: Any move of the rook on f6 opens your queen's diagonal to the black king. Which rook square leaves the black queen with two duties?
ex.dc.HAwiT.solution: 31.Rxf7+! captures the pawn and opens the diagonal of the queen on e5 to the king on h8: it is a discovered check. The only answer is 31...Qxe5: Black captures the piece giving check, but that capture costs them the defence of the rook on f8, because the queen leaves b8. 32.Rxf8# is mate, because the rook on g3 guards g7. With 31.Rxf5+?, the black queen also captures on e5, and you have no mate.
ex.dc.XPg39: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.dc.XPg39.hint: The knight on f6 stands between your queen and the black king. Which knight move forces the king to move?
ex.dc.XPg39.solution: 27.Nxd5+! captures the pawn with check and opens the diagonal of the queen on g5 to the king on e7: it is a double check, and the king must move. After 27...Kf8, 28.Qxd8+ captures the rook, which was left undefended. With 27.Nd7+?, only the queen gives check, and the king captures the knight.
part.intermezzo.title: In-between move
part.intermezzo.summary: Before recapturing, look for a check or a capture the opponent has to answer: the recapture can wait one move.
ex.im.6bMdO: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.im.6bMdO.hint: The white queen has just captured on d8. Before recapturing, look at what your pieces can capture.
ex.im.6bMdO.solution: 16...Bxh6+! The bishop captures the bishop on h6 with check, before the rook recaptures the queen. After 17.Kb1 Rxd8, Black is a piece up. With 16...Rxd8?, 17.Bxg7 trades the bishops, and the game is level.
ex.im.PS5YJ: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.PS5YJ.hint: The black rook has just captured on b7. Look at the other black rook before recapturing.
ex.im.PS5YJ.solution: 30.Qxe8+! The queen captures the rook on e8 with check. After 30...Nf8 31.Nxb7, the knight recaptures on b7, and White is a rook up. With 30.Qxb7? or 30.Nxb7?, the rook on e8 stays alive, and the game is level.
ex.im.gw4Qd: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.gw4Qd.hint: The black bishop has just captured on e5. Before recapturing, look for a move that forces an answer.
ex.im.gw4Qd.solution: 18.Bxe6+! The bishop captures the bishop on e6 with check. After 18...Kb8 19.dxe5, the pawn recaptures the bishop on e5, and White is a piece up. With 18.dxe5?, the rooks are traded on d1, and the bishop on e6 escapes by capturing the pawn on g4: the game is level.
ex.im.7TWLh: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.7TWLh.hint: The black queen has just captured your queen on d3. Before recapturing, look at the captures that force an answer.
ex.im.7TWLh.solution: 17.Nxe7+! The knight captures the bishop on e7 with check. After 17...Kh8 18.cxd3, the pawn recaptures the queen, and White is a piece up. With 17.cxd3?, the bishop on e7 stays alive, and the game is level.
ex.im.boCHM: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.im.boCHM.hint: The white knight has just captured on e6. Before recapturing, look at the white king's diagonal.
ex.im.boCHM.solution: 14...Bxe3+! The bishop captures the bishop on e3 with check. After 15.Kh1 fxe6, the pawn recaptures the knight, and Black is a piece up. With 14...fxe6?, the bishops are traded on e3, and the game is level.
ex.im.ILAMc: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.im.ILAMc.hint: The white rook has just captured on e7. Before a check, see what it wins.
ex.im.ILAMc.solution: 41...Qxe7! Here the right move is to recapture at once. After 42.Qxe7 Bxe7, Black is a piece up. With 41...Qxd5+?, the queen captures a pawn with check, but after 42.Kf2 the rook on e7 is still alive, and White has a decisive advantage. With 41...Qc2+?, after 42.Re2 the rook on e7 also stays alive.
ex.im.s72iQ: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.im.s72iQ.hint: The white knight has just captured on c6. Before recapturing, see who defends it.
ex.im.s72iQ.solution: 28...Nxc5! The white knight on c6 is defended by the rook on c5. The black knight captures that defender, and after 29.bxc5, 29...Qxc6 captures the knight, now undefended. With 28...Qxc6?, the rook on c5 captures the queen.
ex.im.oFFMA: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.im.oFFMA.hint: The white bishop has just captured on d5. Before recapturing, see who defends it.
ex.im.oFFMA.solution: 13...Nxc3! The white bishop on d5 is defended by the knight on c3. The knight on e4 captures that defender, and after 14.bxc3, 14...Qxd5 captures the bishop, now undefended. With 13...Qxd5?, the knight on c3 captures the queen. With 13...Bxf3?, after 14.Qxf3 Nxc3, the bishop escapes with 15.Bxc6, attacking the rook on a8, and White is better.
